title: Find Target Indices After Sorting Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a target element, identify indices where nums[i] equals the target after sorting nums in non-decreasing order.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and a target element, identify indices where nums[i] equals the target after sorting nums in non-decreasing order. Return these indices in sorted order, or an empty list if no such indices exist.
constraints: After conceptual nondecreasing sorting, return every index occupied by target.
Return indices in increasing order, or an empty list when target is absent.
hints: Sorting is unnecessary when only the target block boundaries are needed.
Count values smaller than target and values equal to target.
In sorted order all smaller values precede exactly the equal values, so that interval contains precisely every target index.
editorial: In sorted order all smaller values precede exactly the equal values, so that interval contains precisely every target index.

tests.explanation: Two values are smaller than neither target? After sorting, the two target values occupy indices one and two.
Four is absent, so no sorted index qualifies.
